evidence.citation: Wayne E. Lee, Empires and Indigenes (2011); Daniel K. Richter, The Ordeal of the Longhouse (1992).
evidence.note: Supports confederated war parties, woodland ambush, fortified communities, canoe logistics, and selective firearm adoption.

evidence.citation: Ross Hassig, Aztec Warfare (1988); Ross Hassig, War and Society in Ancient Mesoamerica (1992).
evidence.note: Supports city levies, specialist warrior societies, missile troops, cotton armor, fortifications, and distinct Maya and Purépecha practice.

evidence.citation: Terence N. D'Altroy, The Incas (2014); John Hyslop, The Inka Road System (1984).
evidence.note: Supports sling formations, highland campaigning, state logistics, runners, roads, and Pacific balsa transport.

evidence.citation: William F. Keegan and Corinne L. Hofman, The Caribbean before Columbus (2017).
evidence.note: Supports Taíno and Kalinago canoe mobility, maritime exchange, boarding, and amphibious raiding.

evidence.citation: Matthew Restall, Beyond Black and Red (2015); David J. Weber, Bárbaros (2005).
evidence.note: Supports regional forest warfare and historically contingent adoption of horses, firearms, and artillery after contact rather than in the 1450 baseline.

evidence.citation: Geoffrey Parker, The Military Revolution (2nd ed., 1996).
evidence.note: Pike-and-shot, artillery, drill, fortification, and fiscal constraints in early modern Europe.

evidence.citation: N. A. M. Rodger, The Command of the Ocean (2004).
evidence.note: Sailing battle fleets, naval administration, manpower, and ship-of-the-line development.

evidence.citation: Gabor Agoston, Guns for the Sultan (2005).
evidence.note: Ottoman firearms, artillery logistics, Janissaries, and military institutions.
South Asian cavalry, gunpowder forces, logistics, and regional military labor markets.

evidence.citation: John Thornton, Warfare in Atlantic Africa, 1500–1800 (1999).
evidence.note: African infantry, cavalry, firearms adoption, organization, and environmental constraints.

evidence.citation: K. N. Chaudhuri, Trade and Civilisation in the Indian Ocean (1985).
evidence.note: Indian Ocean ports, provisioning, dhow traffic, and long-distance shipping.

evidence.citation: Kenneth Swope, A Dragon's Head and a Serpent's Tail (2009); Stephen Turnbull, Samurai Warfare (1996).
evidence.note: Supports Ming firearms formations, East Asian fortification warfare, Japanese retinues, and sixteenth-century matchlock adoption.
Supports Joseon gunpowder defenses and multiple-arrow hwacha batteries without projecting later artillery backward.
Supports Mongol and Jurchen mounted archery, steppe logistics, and banner-based frontier forces.

evidence.citation: Michael W. Charney, Southeast Asian Warfare, 1300-1900 (2004).
evidence.note: Supports elephant corps, mandala levies, gunpowder, riverine warfare, fortifications, and maritime raiding.

evidence.citation: Anthony Reid, Southeast Asia in the Age of Commerce, 1450-1680 (1988-1993).
evidence.note: Supports lancaran, kora-kora, swivel guns, boarding forces, ports, and archipelagic trade.

evidence.citation: Geoffrey Irwin, The Prehistoric Exploration and Colonisation of the Pacific (1992); Ben Finney, Voyage of Rediscovery (1994).
evidence.note: Supports ocean-going double-hulled canoes, wayfinding, reef navigation, and long-distance voyaging.

evidence.citation: Patrick V. Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2000).
evidence.note: Supports island defense, chiefly warrior formations, amphibious movement, and regional war canoes.
